AmazonSES.PluginDescription: Send all Matomo emails through the Amazon SES API v2.
AmazonSES.TestRecipientHelp: If your SES account is still in the sandbox, the recipient must be a verified identity.
AmazonSES.TestSent: Test email sent to %1$s. SES MessageId: %2$s
AmazonSES.TestEmailSubject: Matomo test email via Amazon SES
AmazonSES.TestEmailBody: Hello! This test email was sent from %s through Amazon SES. If you are reading it, the AmazonSES plugin works.
AmazonSES.InvalidTestRecipient: Please enter a valid email address.
AmazonSES.EmailsDisabled: Emails are disabled in config.ini.php ([General] emails_enabled = 0): Matomo will not send any email.
AmazonSES.TransportNotActive: Another plugin replaced the mail transport: the AmazonSES transport is not active.
AmazonSES.SettingRegionHelp: Region of your SES account. Your sender identity must be verified in this region. Other regions can be set in config.ini.php ([AmazonSES] region = "...").
AmazonSES.SettingAccessKeyIdHelp: Leave empty to use the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable or an IAM role (ECS task role, EC2 instance profile). The key needs the ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions.
AmazonSES.SettingAccessKeyIdInvalid: The access key ID should only contain uppercase letters and digits (e.g. AKIA...).
AmazonSES.SettingSecretAccessKeyHelp: Stored in the Matomo database like the SMTP password. For production we recommend IAM roles or environment variables.
AmazonSES.SettingConfigurationSetHelp: Name of an SES configuration set, e.g. to publish bounces and complaints to SNS or CloudWatch.
AmazonSES.SettingConfigurationSetInvalid: The configuration set name can only contain letters, digits, dashes and underscores (max 64 characters).
AmazonSES.SettingSenderEmailHelp: Overrides the Matomo 'from' address. It must be a verified identity (address or domain) in Amazon SES. Leave empty to use the Matomo noreply address.
